speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. I see you are presenting with rapid breathing, liver enlargement, and pitting edema. To understand the cause of this fluid overload and respiratory distress, have you noticed any changes in your urine output or swelling in your legs recently?

speaker: Patient
text: 3-year-old child. The parents report that the child appears unwell and has been breathing rapidly. They also noticed some swelling in the child's legs but no fever, cough, or previous similar episodes. The child's appetite has diminished over the past few days. No recent illnesses or hospitalizations. The child is fully immunized.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Nephrotic syndrome.

The child's presentation of rapid breathing, liver enlargement, pitting edema, and diminished urine output in the absence of fever or respiratory infection strongly suggests nephrotic syndrome leading to fluid overload and potential heart failure. I will proceed with immediate testing to confirm this diagnosis and assess renal function.

REQUEST TEST: Urinalysis with microscopy
REQUEST TEST: Serum albumin and total protein
REQUEST TEST: Serum creatinine and BUN
REQUEST TEST: Serum electrolytes
REQUEST TEST: Liver function tests (ALT, AST, ALP, Bilirubin)
REQUEST TEST: Serum complement levels (C3, C4)
